candidate.title: MIPSTR
candidate.scope: MIPSTR, specifically the assigned poster row showing smMIP capture of STR loci, copying the targeted STR, amplification/sequencing, and the two illustrative readout contexts (between individuals and within an individual). The 2015 Carlson et al. implementation resolves the probe chemistry and readout association. The adjacent smMIP, MDA/IMS-MDA/MIDAS rows and right-edge cytosine chemistry are contextual, not alternative MIPSTR workflows. This is schematic architecture, not a complete protocol.

states.label: STR-targeting single-molecule molecular inversion probes (smMIPs)
features: One oligonucleotide carries locus-specific STR-flanking targeting arms, a common PCR/sequencing-priming backbone, and a 12-nt degenerate molecular tag.
The tag identifies an individual capture event; it is distinct from a sample index.
The drawing uses a looped probe and a red segment labeled Degenerate molecular tag; the hybridized probe is not yet the closed capture product.

One targeting arm is the primer for polymerase extension (extension arm). Ligation closes the circle at the other targeting arm (ligation arm).

states.label: Sample-associated STR target and molecular-tag reads
features: Paired sequencing observations link the captured STR and targeting-arm sequence to its degenerate tag; a separate index read identifies the sample.
The paper assigns the forward read to the ligation arm and STR target, and the reverse read to the degenerate tag and extension arm.
Tag-defined groups represent independent capture events, not identified individual cells.

In the reported sequencing implementation, target-spanning reads constrain STR length assessment (approximately 180 bp); large expansions can omit part or all of the extension targeting arm. Capture alone does not guarantee an informative repeat-unit call.

evidence.locator: MIPSTR row, middle-right: outgoing arrow from Copy target STR; Amplify and sequence

evidence.quote: MIPSTR libraries were sequenced using 250-bp forward reads paired with 50-bp reverse reads on the Illumina MiSeq platform. The 250-bp forward reads spanned the ∼20-bp ligation targeting arm followed by 200 bp of target sequence (STR sequence and unique flanking sequence) and ∼20 bp extension targeting arm (large STR expansions will be missing some or all of the extension targeting arm). MIPSTR can assess STRs up to ∼180 bp in length, considerably longer than the STRs currently assessed from common Illumina 100-bp whole-genome-sequencing data. The 50-bp reverse reads spanned the 12-bp degenerate tag, which identifies each specific MIP molecule, and the extension targeting arm (Fig. 1A).

We collected one 250-bp forward read to determine sequence of the ligation arm and STR target locus, one 50-bp reverse read to determine the sequence of the degenerate tag and extension arm, and one 8-bp read to determine the sample index sequence.

For each tag-defined read group (i.e., reads containing the same MIP tag), we assumed that the mode of called unit numbers across reads is the true allele for this capture event (Fig. 3). STR unit number variation within a tag-defined read group is considered technical error (Fig. 3; Supplemental Table 1). However, unit number variation observed among different MIP molecules, each representing independent capture events, is potentially the result of heterozygosity, somatic variation, or duplication (Figs. 1C, 3).

states.label: Locus- and sample-resolved STR calls grouped by capture tag
features: Locus identity derives from targeting-arm sequence; locus-specific synthetic STR references resolve repeat-unit number.
Reads sharing a degenerate tag within a locus/sample form a capture-event group.
The mode STR unit number within each group is taken as the capture-event allele; within-group dispersion measures technical variation.

evidence.quote: We sorted reads according to their MIP targeting arms, and for each MIP, used BWA (Li and Durbin 2009) to map its corresponding reads to a set of synthetic reference sequences designed specifically for each targeted STR (Fig. 1D).

For each tag-defined read group (i.e., reads containing the same MIP tag), we assumed that the mode of called unit numbers across reads is the true allele for this capture event (Fig. 3). STR unit number variation within a tag-defined read group is considered technical error (Fig. 3; Supplemental Table 1). However, unit number variation observed among different MIP molecules, each representing independent capture events, is potentially the result of heterozygosity, somatic variation, or duplication (Figs. 1C, 3).

We then sorted the STR genotype calls by the degenerate tag on the paired reverse read from which they derived. We required an exact match of the 12-bp degenerate tag for reads to be grouped into a tag-defined read group. We then called the mode STR unit number of each tag-defined read group as the genotype of that DNA molecule.

states.label: Between-individual STR genotype variation
features: The Strain I versus Strain II cartoon illustrates comparison of STR repeat lengths across individuals.
Sample-specific germline STR unit-number calls can be compared across individuals; this panel is a readout context, not another chemical product.

states.label: Within-individual STR allele diversity and candidate somatic variation
features: The two Strain I cartoons illustrate distinct STR alleles within one individual.
Concordant allele support across independent capture tags can distinguish candidate biological variants from within-tag amplification stutter.
Between-tag differences can also reflect heterozygosity or duplicated loci; tag differences alone do not uniquely prove somatic origin or assign a variant to a cell.

operations.label: Targeted capture of STR loci by smMIPs (MIPSTR)
operations.description: Combine target genomic DNA and STR-targeting tagged probes so that locus-specific arms hybridize to STR flanking sequence; the output is a probe-template complex poised to copy the STR.
operations.mechanism: Sequence-specific hybridization of the extension and ligation targeting arms.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a physical association between an STR locus and one tagged capture probe before amplification.

operations.label: Copy target STR
operations.description: Copy the genomic interval between the bound probe arms and close the probe into a circular STR-containing capture product. The copied interval changes the probe from a bound capture reagent into the template for library amplification.
operations.mechanism: One targeting arm primes polymerase extension; ligation at the other arm closes the circle. The figure label is retained, and the primary Fig. 1A caption establishes extension and ligation.
operations.information_effect: The circular probe product, rather than untouched genomic DNA, carries the copied STR allele physically linked to the degenerate capture tag.

operations.label: Amplify and sequence
operations.description: Amplify the captured probe products into an indexed sequencing library and read the STR-containing products together with molecular-tag and sample-index information. The figure combines these transformations in one block.
operations.mechanism: PCR from the common probe backbone uses a common forward primer and indexed reverse primer; paired target/tag sequencing and an index read establish the readout interface. The library state is an internal physical carrier of this combined block, not a separately drawn branch.
operations.information_effect: Many reads can descend from one capture event. Copies retain the capture tag, while sample indexing permits individual assignment. Amplification can introduce STR stutter, so raw read diversity is not itself biological allele diversity.

operations.label: Interpret STR reads and tag-defined capture events
operations.description: Resolve sequenced STR products into locus-specific repeat-unit calls and capture-event groups, supplying the information needed by both depicted readout contexts. This interpretive interface is reported by the primary paper rather than drawn as a separate poster box.

operations.information_effect: Retains the sample/locus/tag association; separates technical dispersion within one capture-event group from differences supported by independent captures.

operations.label: Natural variation between individuals
operations.description: Compare sample-specific STR genotypes across genetically distinct individuals, represented by Strain I and Strain II; the output is between-individual repeat-unit variation.
operations.mechanism: Compare locus-specific STR allele calls after assignment to individual samples.
operations.information_effect: Reads from distinct individuals support germline STR genotype comparisons. This is one interpretation of the captured/sequenced library, not a material transfer into the adjacent within-individual panel.

operations.label: Somatic variation within an individual
operations.description: Within one individual, compare STR alleles supported by independent tagged capture events while using within-tag variation to assess amplification stutter; report supported allele diversity and candidate somatic variants.
operations.mechanism: The tag-defined read-group mode estimates the captured allele. Independent groups supporting an alternate allele provide evidence for within-sample variation; heterozygosity and locus duplication remain alternative biological explanations.
operations.information_effect: The poster labels this somatic variation, but the primary paper makes the inference conditional: between-capture differences are potentially heterozygosity, somatic variation, or duplication. Tags identify capture events, not cell lineages.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card title and the MIPSTR row delimit a single method. smMIP is the probe/capture component embedded in MIPSTR, not an additional target workflow. The matching catalogue page is headed MIPSTR: Targeted Capture of STR Loci by smMIPs and reproduces the same copy/amplify/readout labels. The primary paper resolves tagged circle formation and the sequencing-to-readout interface. The two terminal comparisons are alternative readout contexts using appropriately assigned sample/capture groups, not successive chemical stages and not a depicted pooling operation.
